  - resources/23-sql-best-practices-olap.md §3.1D — ADDED a single grep-findable DO-NOT-WRITE blockquote IMMEDIATELY AFTER the §3.1D `max_by` canonical worked example (line 500) and BEFORE the 'Picking between' subsection. Keyword anchors: 'end of week balance, end of day reading, latest value per group not largest, max_by vs MAX, value as of latest timestamp, last reading per bucket, last count of the day not highest, balance at end of week not maximum balance, end-of-week balance, end-of-day reading, latest status per bucket'. The rule: when the question is about 'the value AS OF the latest time' (end-of-week balance, end-of-day reading, last status per bucket), use `max_by(value, ts)` — NOT `MAX(value)`. WRONG `SELECT account_id, date_trunc('week', posted_date) AS week_start, MAX(balance) AS balance_eow FROM ledger GROUP BY ...`; RIGHT `... max_by(balance, posted_date) AS balance_eow ...`. Same fix for last-count-of-day (`max_by(count_val, recorded_at)`), closing price (`max_by(price, traded_at)`), final status (`max_by(status, event_ts)`). Mnemonic: 'if the answer must be the value at a specific point in time, use max_by(value, time); reserve MAX(value) for the maximum across the period — peak balance, peak CPU, high-water-mark.' Cites trino.io/docs/467/functions/aggregate.html — `max_by(x, y) -> [same as x]`: 'Returns the value of x associated with the maximum value of y over all input values.'

SELECT grammar at trino.io/docs/current/sql/select.html — GROUP BY accepts column refs / grouping-set lists, not aggregate functions. (2) max_by semantics — verified at trino.io/docs/467/functions/aggregate.html: `max_by(x, y)` returns 'the value of x associated with the maximum value of y over all input values' (Trino docs verbatim) — this is the value-AT-the-MAX-y, NOT the MAX of x.
